subject: GapBridge: compatibility pass and proposed experiment plan
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@gapbridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up and next steps from today's call

Hi Ethan —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

- What we heard:
  - Primary goal: migrate latency-sensitive inference for search/rerank to a low-cost, predictable runtime.
  - Must maintain OpenAI-compatible API surface for minimal engineering lift (prompts + SDK).
  - Key non-functional: 50ms p50 for short queries, predictable token billing, and SOC2 evidence for procurement.

- Immediate asks from GapBridge:
  1) A short smoke test plan we can run against a representative prompt set (your sample prompts you shared).
  2) Clarify API parity gaps you saw during the trial calls (if any) — prompt/response shape, streaming, function call edge cases.
  3) Estimate of delta in token billing and examples causing token variance.

Attached is a compact test plan that covers RTT, streaming correctness, and a small prompt-diff harness. Proposed timeline:
- You run the smoke tests this week and share a run log (we can help run it if preferred).
- Redwood runs a parallel compatibility pass on the same prompts and returns diffs/latency samples by Friday.

Next-step ask: can you confirm who will own the smoke test on GapBridge and whether Procurement needs a SOC2 artifact in parallel?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-gapbridge-initial-test-plan.pdf (6 pages), gapbridge-sample-prompts.jsonl (30 prompts)

From: Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@gapbridge.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-06T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up and next steps from today's call

Tessa —

Appreciate the clear recap. We're aligned. Quick answers:

- I'll own the smoke test on our side; procurement asked for SOC2 Type II evidence but can accept a scoped controls summary while legal wraps up the SOW.
- Early trialing (using our dev key) showed two small differences:
  1) Streaming chunk boundaries — a few of our streaming clients assume fixed "chunk" sizes and saw slightly different micro-timing. Not blocking, but worth validating.
  2) Token accounting: one prompt that concatenates system+user caused a +7 token delta in Redwood vs our current provider; need examples to confirm whether it's prompt-encoding or pre-tokenization normalization.

We'll run your plan Thursday and upload logs. One ask back: can Redwood run a small "SDK swap" test where we point a staging service at Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoint (same SDK call) for 24 hours and surface OOM/retry behavior? That will help stakeholders see the friction of changing the backend.

Ethan
Ethan Ross
Head of Platform Engineering, GapBridge

-----

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-07T10:25:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: GapBridge compatibility pass — action items

Ben / Marissa — forwarding GapBridge's notes (below). Two asks for Redwood team:

1) Ben — can you scope the 24h SDK-swap run and list what telemetry we need to capture to demonstrate no behavioral regressions? Focus: streaming timing, token accounting, retry/429 behavior, and memory faults. Estimate needed infra and whether Dedicated dev pool is required.

2) Marissa — please draft a short controls summary for SOC2 that we can share with Procurement immediately (1 page). They don't need the full report yet.

I've attached the test plan they will run and the sample prompts. Let's aim to have Ben's telemetry checklist + Marissa's controls summary by Wednesday (2026-11-11).

Thanks —
Tessa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: GapBridge compatibility pass — action items

Tessa / Marissa —

Plan and owners below.

Telemetry / scope for 24h SDK-swap (owner: Ben)
- Capture p50/p95/p99 latency for token counts [0-128], [129-512], [>512] (sample every 1s)
- Streaming trace: record chunk timestamps and sizes, and the initial response delta (first-byte time)
- Token accounting: log raw input bytes, tokenized token counts (Redwood tokenizer) and compare with raw provider counts — include raw examples that show deltas
- Error taxonomy: collect 5xx, 4xx, connection resets, and any OOMs with stack/hostname
- Cost sample: calculate per-request token delta * token price estimate and provide sample table
- Duration and infra: need a small Dedicated dev pool with 1x A10 equivalent for the 24h run; infra cost estimate ~ $75 for the run (we can absorb for a PO if needed)

Deliverables + ETA:
- Ben: telemetry checklist + minimal harness to run the SDK-swap by 2026-11-11 EOD
- Marissa: SOC2 controls summary + a one-page procurement note by 2026-11-11 EOD
- Tessa: coordinate upload location for the GapBridge logs (I'll provide a signed URL)

I'll start building the harness today and ping infra for a short-lived dev pool.

—Ben

Attachments mentioned earlier: redwood-gapbridge-initial-test-plan.pdf
